pool.text: Cholas defeated Western Gangas under Rajendra Chola I and captured the region.
Hoysala king Vishnuvardhana defeated the Cholas in the Battle of Talakad.
Kempe Gowda I established a mud fort considered the foundation of modern Bengaluru.
Adil Shahi army defeated Kempe Gowda III, making the city Shahaji's jagir.
Shahaji ordered the reconstruction of the town and built large fortifications.
The Cubbon Park was established as a large park in the heart of the city.
Labour unrest in Binny Mills resulted in a baton charge and police firing.
Bengaluru's reputation as the Garden City began with silver jubilee celebrations.
Ramayya established the Bangalore Press and launched the Kannada newspaper Tayi Nadu.
Notable communal disturbances occurred after a Ganesh idol was removed.
Telephone services were introduced for communication across the city.
The first flight between Bengaluru and Mumbai took off.
The City and the Cantonment merged to form the Bengaluru City Corporation.
All India Radio started AM broadcasting from its Bengaluru station.
Karnataka Rajyotsava marks the formation of Karnataka state.
The Bangalore Amateur Radio Club, an amateur radio club, was established.
Water supply is provided by the Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board.
The Government of Karnataka constituted the Bangalore Development Authority.
A major fire broke out at Venus Circus where more than 92 people died.
The government-run Doordarshan broadcasts television channels from its Bengaluru centre.
